breakfast.name: Kaukau (Sweet Potato)
instructions: Boil or roast sweet potatoes in coals
Season with salt
breakfast.description: Roasted sweet potato — PNG's primary staple.

breakfast.name: Sago Pancakes
instructions: Mix sago with water into thick paste
Cook on hot stones or griddle
Serve with coconut cream
breakfast.description: Pancakes made from sago palm starch.

breakfast.name: Boiled Kaukau (Sweet Potato Breakfast)
ingredients: Kaukau (sweet potato — PNG's staple, multiple varieties)
instructions: Kaukau (sweet potato) is PNG's most important food — the highlands staple for millennia
PNG's highlands are one of the world's independent centers of agriculture — 10,000+ years
Over 5,000 varieties of sweet potato are grown in PNG — more than almost anywhere
The kaukau gardens are the foundation of Highland society — land = kaukau = life
Boil kaukau until tender — the flesh can be orange, purple, white, or yellow depending on variety
Serve plain or with coconut cream — the simplicity is the point
Highland communities eat kaukau for every meal — breakfast, lunch, dinner
The kaukau is roasted in earth ovens or boiled — both ancient techniques
Sweet potato replaced taro as the primary Highland crop centuries ago
breakfast.description: PNG's foundation food — kaukau (sweet potato, 5,000+ varieties grown in PNG) boiled until tender. PNG's highlands are one of the world's independent centers of agriculture — 10,000+ years of cultivation. Highland communities eat kaukau for every meal. The kaukau garden is the foundation of Highland society — land = kaukau = life.

breakfast.name: Saksak (Sago Pancake)
ingredients: Sago flour (from processed sago palm pith)
instructions: Sago is the staple starch of PNG's lowland and coastal regions — particularly the Sepik River area
Processing sago: the palm trunk is felled, the pith is pounded and washed to extract starch
Sago processing is labor-intensive — the starch is washed out with water, settled, dried
Mix sago flour with water into a dough — form into thick pancakes
Cook on a flat stone or pan — the sago sets into a dense, slightly translucent cake
Serve with coconut cream — the fat enriches the relatively neutral sago
Sago is NOT nutritionally rich (mostly starch) but provides critical calories
In lowland PNG, sago palms grow wild in swampland — a reliable food source
The Sepik River communities are sago cultures — the palm is central to their way of life
breakfast.description: PNG's lowland staple — sago flour (pounded and washed from sago palm pith, labor-intensive processing) mixed into thick pancakes and cooked until dense and slightly translucent. Served with coconut cream. Sago is the Sepik River communities' foundation — the palm grows wild in swampland. Not nutritionally rich (mostly starch) but provides critical calories in lowland PNG.

lunch.name: Mumu (Earth Oven Feast)
instructions: Dig pit, heat stones in fire
Wrap food in banana leaves
Layer over hot stones
Cover with earth
Cook 3 hours
Uncover and feast communally
lunch.description: PNG's traditional earth oven feast — meat and vegetables cooked by hot stones.

lunch.name: Fish in Coconut
instructions: Simmer coconut milk with onion and ginger
Add fish, cook 15 min
Squeeze lime
Serve with kaukau

lunch.name: Kokoda (Fijian-Style Raw Fish Salad)
instructions: Kokoda is a Pacific Island raw fish salad — found across PNG's coastal communities
Similar to Fijian kokoda and other Pacific Island ceviche traditions
The fish is marinated in lime juice until opaque — the acid 'cooks' the proteins
Add thick coconut cream — the richness balances the acid
Mixed with fresh tomato, cucumber, onion, and chili
This is coastal PNG food — the reef provides the fish
The coconut cream added to the lime-cured fish is the Pacific distinction from South American ceviche
PNG's coastline is enormous — coastal cultures have diverse fishing traditions
Kokoda is celebration food — served at community gatherings and sing-sings
lunch.description: PNG's coastal ceviche — fresh reef fish lime-cured until opaque, mixed with thick coconut cream (the Pacific distinction from South American ceviche), tomato, cucumber, and chili. Coastal PNG food from communities along the enormous coastline. Celebration food served at sing-sings (community gatherings). The reef provides.

lunch.name: Banana and Taro Soup
instructions: Green banana and taro soup is a common daily meal across PNG
Both banana and taro are traditional PNG crops — cultivated for millennia
The green banana is starchy, not sweet — it cooks like a potato
Simmer taro and green banana in coconut milk until both soften
Add fish or chicken for protein — the coconut broth enriches everything
Ginger adds warmth — it grows wild across PNG's tropical lowlands
This soup is sustenance — simple, filling, made from garden staples
PNG has the highest linguistic diversity on earth (800+ languages) — food traditions vary enormously
But the starch + coconut milk + protein formula is shared across many communities
lunch.description: PNG daily sustenance — starchy green banana and taro simmered in coconut milk with ginger and optional fish or chicken. Both crops have been cultivated in PNG for millennia. PNG has 800+ languages and enormous cultural diversity, but the starch + coconut milk + protein formula is shared across many communities.

lunch.name: Tin Fish and Rice
ingredients: Canned fish (mackerel or tuna — widely available)
instructions: Canned fish and rice is one of PNG's most common everyday meals
Canned fish became a protein staple because of its shelf stability in tropical heat
In remote communities without refrigeration, canned fish is reliable protein
Sauté onion and garlic, add canned fish, season with soy sauce and chili
Serve over boiled rice — the combination is simple, cheap, filling
This is not traditional PNG food — it represents the modern PNG diet transition
The shift from garden food (kaukau, taro, sago) to store-bought food is ongoing
In urban PNG (Port Moresby, Lae), rice and tin fish is everyday lunch
The dish reflects PNG's position between traditional food sovereignty and globalized food systems
lunch.description: Modern PNG's everyday meal — canned fish (shelf-stable protein in tropical heat) sautéed with onion, garlic, soy sauce, and chili, served over rice. Represents the ongoing PNG diet transition from garden food (kaukau, taro, sago) to store-bought staples. In urban Port Moresby and Lae, this is everyday lunch. Between traditional food sovereignty and globalized food systems.

dinner.name: Tulip (Aibika) Greens
instructions: Wash aibika leaves
Simmer in coconut cream with onion
Cook until soft and thick
dinner.description: Aibika greens in coconut cream — PNG's most common vegetable.

dinner.name: Canned Corned Beef and Rice
instructions: Cook rice
Sauté onion and tomato
Add corned beef, heat through
Serve with rice
dinner.description: A pragmatic PNG dinner — canned beef is widely used.

dinner.name: Smoked Fish
ingredients: Whole fish (reef fish or river fish)
instructions: Smoking fish is one of PNG's oldest preservation techniques — essential in the tropics
Without refrigeration, smoking extends fish life from hours to days or weeks
The fish is gutted, salted, and placed over a slow hardwood or coconut-husk smoke
The smoking takes hours — low heat, dense smoke, patience
The result: firm, deeply flavored, preserved fish that can be stored or transported
In coastal villages, rows of fish smoking over open racks is a common sight
Smoked fish is traded inland — coastal communities trade fish for highland kaukau
This coastal-highland trade network is ancient — food exchange across PNG's geography
The smoking technique varies by community — different woods, different methods
Smoked fish is eaten as-is or added to soups and stews for flavor
dinner.description: PNG's ancient preservation — whole fish smoked over hardwood or coconut husks for hours, extending shelf life in the tropics from hours to weeks. Coastal villages trade smoked fish inland for highland kaukau — an ancient exchange network across PNG's geography. Each community has its own smoking technique. Eaten straight or added to soups and stews for deep smoky flavor.

dinner.name: Chicken Stew with Greens
ingredients: Leafy greens (aibika — PNG's most common green vegetable)
instructions: Aibika is PNG's most commonly eaten green — a tropical shrub with edible leaves
The leaves are slightly mucilaginous (like okra) — they add body to stews
Chicken stewed in coconut milk with aibika greens is comfort food across PNG
Brown chicken pieces, add onion, garlic, ginger
Add coconut milk and simmer until chicken is tender
Add aibika leaves — they wilt quickly and thicken the sauce slightly
The mucilaginous texture is valued, not avoided — it's the right texture in PNG cooking
Aibika grows easily in PNG's climate — planted in home gardens everywhere
The combination of chicken + coconut + greens is the everyday dinner formula
dinner.description: PNG comfort food — chicken simmered in coconut milk with aibika (PNG's most common green, slightly mucilaginous like okra, adding body to the stew). The mucilaginous texture is valued, not avoided — the right texture in PNG cooking. Aibika grows in home gardens everywhere across PNG's tropical climate. Chicken + coconut + greens: the everyday dinner formula.

dinner.name: Pork and Kaukau (Celebration Feast)
ingredients: Greens (kumu — general term for cooked leafy greens)
instructions: Pork and kaukau together represent the PNG celebration meal — feast food
Pigs have enormous cultural importance in PNG — they are wealth, ceremony, exchange
In many Highland societies, pigs are given names and raised by women
The pig kill for a feast is a significant event — it marks weddings, alliances, mourning
Simmer pork until very tender — the fat renders into the broth
Add kaukau pieces and greens — cook until everything is soft
The coconut cream enriches the stew — the fat from the pork compounds it
This is hearty, sustaining, communal food — served at gatherings
The combination pork + kaukau = the most culturally significant PNG meal
The 'mumu' (earth oven feast) version cooks everything in banana-leaf packages underground
dinner.description: PNG's celebration feast — pork (culturally significant: pigs are wealth, ceremony, exchange in many Highland societies) simmered with kaukau (sweet potato) and greens in coconut cream. The pig kill for a feast marks weddings, alliances, mourning. The mumu (earth oven) version cooks everything underground in banana-leaf packages. Pork + kaukau = PNG's most culturally significant meal.

snacks.name: Buai (Betel Nut)
instructions: Crack betel nut
Dip in lime powder
Chew with mustard stick
snacks.description: Betel nut — PNG's traditional stimulant, chewed everywhere.

snacks.name: Roasted Corn
instructions: Corn roasted over open flame is sold at markets and roadside across PNG
The corn chars slightly on the outside — the smoke flavor is the point
In PNG's tropical climate, corn grows well and provides quick calories
The charred-sweet flavor of fire-roasted corn is universal — found worldwide
In PNG, the open fire is still the primary cooking method in many communities
The simplicity is everything: corn + fire + salt
Sold at markets in Goroka, Mt. Hagen, Port Moresby — a few kina per cob
Roasted corn is one of the few snacks available in remote communities
snacks.description: PNG's market snack — corn on the cob roasted over open flame until slightly charred and smoky. In many PNG communities, open fire is still the primary cooking method. Sold at markets in Goroka, Mt. Hagen, Port Moresby for a few kina. The simplicity: corn + fire + salt.

snacks.name: Fried Sago Balls
instructions: Sago flour mixed with grated coconut and sugar, shaped into balls, fried golden
A lowland snack — sago is the Sepik and coastal communities' staple
The coconut adds fat and flavor to the otherwise neutral sago
The frying adds crunch — the balls are crispy outside, chewy inside
Fried sago balls are sold at markets and at small roadside stalls
The sago palm provides not just food but also building material (thatch, walls)
Sago cultures in PNG depend on the palm for multiple aspects of life
snacks.description: PNG lowland snack — sago flour mixed with grated coconut and sugar, shaped into balls and fried until crispy outside and chewy inside. Sago is the Sepik and coastal communities' staple — the palm provides food, thatch, and building material. Sold at markets and roadside stalls.

snacks.name: Buai (Betel Nut)
ingredients: Betel nut (areca nut — the fruit of the areca palm)
instructions: Buai (betel nut) is PNG's most widespread social custom — chewed daily by millions
It is NOT a food but a mild stimulant — chewed for the energizing, warming effect
The betel nut is bitten in half, dipped in slaked lime powder (kambang), chewed with daka (mustard stick)
The lime catalyzes the alkaloid release — the mouth fills with bright red juice
The red-stained teeth and lips of buai chewers are visible across PNG
Buai markets are significant economic activity — the nut is traded nationally
Chewing buai is social — offered as greeting, hospitality, friendship
The World Health Organization classifies betel nut as a carcinogen — health concerns are serious
Despite health warnings, buai remains deeply culturally embedded
Port Moresby's streets are stained red from spat buai juice — the city's distinctive mark
snacks.description: PNG's most widespread social custom — betel nut (areca nut) chewed with slaked lime and mustard stick for a mild stimulant effect. NOT food but deeply culturally embedded: offered as greeting and hospitality, chewed daily by millions. Stains teeth and lips bright red. Buai markets are significant economic activity. WHO classifies it as a carcinogen, but cultural attachment persists. Port Moresby's streets are stained red.

desserts.name: Baked Banana
instructions: Wrap bananas in banana leaves or foil
Bake over coals 20 min
Open, drizzle with coconut cream and sugar

desserts.name: Roasted Banana with Coconut
instructions: Roasting bananas over fire is ancient in PNG — the simplest dessert
Ripe bananas become caramelized and intensely sweet when roasted
The thick-skinned PNG banana varieties hold up to roasting without falling apart
Drizzle with coconut cream — the fat enriches the caramelized fruit
Optional sugar or honey, but ripe bananas are often sweet enough
PNG has dozens of banana varieties — each with different flavor, texture, size
Bananas are one of PNG's most important crops — eaten daily in most communities
The sweet, smoky, coconut-enriched banana is comfort food — the original dessert
desserts.description: PNG's original dessert — ripe bananas (thick-skinned varieties that hold up to fire) roasted until caramelized and intensely sweet, drizzled with coconut cream. PNG has dozens of banana varieties, each with different flavor and texture. Bananas are eaten daily across most communities. Sweet, smoky, coconut-enriched — the simplest and most ancient dessert.

desserts.name: Sago Pudding with Banana
instructions: Sago pudding is the lowland sweet — sago starch cooked in coconut milk
Cook sago in coconut milk until it becomes translucent and thick
Mix in mashed ripe banana — the banana sweetens and flavors
The pudding sets as it cools — dense, slightly sticky, sweet
This is the Sepik and coastal communities' dessert — their staple starch made sweet
Sago pudding represents the transformation of subsistence food into celebration food
The coconut milk and banana elevate the neutral sago into something rich and satisfying
desserts.description: PNG lowland dessert — sago starch cooked in coconut milk until translucent and thick, mixed with mashed ripe banana for sweetness. Dense, slightly sticky, satisfying. The Sepik and coastal communities' sweet — subsistence sago transformed into celebration food by coconut milk and banana.

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open coconut
Drink water fresh

drinks.name: Tok Kopi (PNG Coffee)
instructions: Boil water, add coffee
Simmer 3 min
Strain, add sugar
drinks.description: Strong PNG coffee — world-class single origin.

drinks.name: Kulau (Green Coconut Water)
ingredients: Green coconut (young — the water inside is sweet and abundant)
instructions: Kulau is the drink of the tropics — young green coconut water drunk straight from the nut
In PNG's humid tropical climate, coconut water is nature's hydration
The young green coconut is cut open with a machete — the top sliced off
The water inside is sweet, clear, slightly nutty — refreshing in the heat
After drinking, the soft jelly-like meat inside is scooped and eaten with a spoon cut from the shell
Coconut palms grow along PNG's entire coastline — the trees are everywhere
Kulau is free — the palms produce abundantly and the nuts fall naturally
The drink requires no processing, no sugar, no preparation — nature provides
Coconut water has become a global health-drink trend — in PNG it's just the obvious choice
drinks.description: PNG's natural refreshment — young green coconut water drunk straight from the machete-opened nut. Sweet, clear, hydrating in the humid tropical heat. After drinking, scoop and eat the soft jelly-like meat with a shell-spoon. Coconut palms line PNG's entire coastline — the drink is free and abundant. The global coconut water trend discovered what PNG has always known.
